papers.title: Impact of body mass index to functional outcomes in patients after primary total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is a frequently performed orthopedic procedure to relieve pain and restore function in patients with degenerative or traumatic changes of the hip joint. Obesity has been identified as a potential modifier of surgical outcomes, but the literature is conflicting on the effects of obesity on postoperative functional recovery compared to non-obese populations. This study aimed to investigate the influence of preoperative body mass index (BMI) on long-term functional outcomes following primary THA, with a five-year follow-up conducted in South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted involving 30 patients who underwent primary THA at Dr. Wahidin Sudirohusodo Central General Hospital, Makassar, in 2023. Functional outcomes were assessed using the change in Harris hip score (ΔHHS), calculated from preoperative and six-month postoperative evaluations. Statistical analyses included the Shapiro-Wilk test for normality, Spearman’s rank correlation for non-parametric associations, Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests for group comparisons, and multivariate linear regression to identify independent predictors of functional improvement. Results: Samples consisting of 60% female, mean age 56.8±11.0 years; 66.7% obese. Strong negative correlation between BMI and delta HHS (r=-0.949, p<0.001). Significant differences across BMI categories (p<0.001), with obese II showing the poorest outcomes. BMI was the significant primary predictor (-3.417, p<0.001), while age and gender were not. Conclusion: Higher BMI significantly correlates with poorer functional outcomes post-THA. Weight management after THA is crucial for optimizing the patient’s functional outcomes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅关注BMI与THA术后功能评分的临床关联，未涉及任何生物力学建模、应力遮挡或微动分析，与用户研究方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include any biomechanical modeling, finite element analysis, stress shielding, micromotion, or implant design considerations; it is purely a clinical outcome study.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨BMI对THA术后功能恢复的影响。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性队列研究，分析30例THA患者BMI与Harris评分变化的关系。
summary_zh.result: BMI与功能改善呈强负相关，肥胖患者预后较差。
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床随访数据的统计分析。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether preoperative body mass index influences long-term functional recovery after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective cohort study of 30 primary THA patients assessed the association between BMI and change in Harris hip score using correlation and regression analyses.
summary_en.result: Higher BMI was strongly correlated with poorer functional improvement, with BMI being the primary predictor.
summary_en.validation: Clinical validation using six-month postoperative functional scores from a single hospital cohort.

papers.title: Effects of laser power and scanning speed on the forming quality of high-layer-thickness Ti-6Al-4V alloy by selective laser melting

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM工艺参数对高厚度Ti-6Al-4V成形质量的影响，虽未直接涉及生物医学植入物，但其工艺-质量关系对AM生物医学材料的制造优化具有参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not link porous structure to stress shielding or stiffness matching, does not include mechanical testing (fatigue or otherwise), and does not report surface roughness, as-built morphology, or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究激光功率和扫描速度对高厚度Ti-6Al-4V SLM成形质量的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过实验改变激光功率和扫描速度，分析成形件的密度、缺陷和力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 确定了优化工艺参数窗口，改善了成形质量。
summary_zh.validation: 采用实验测试验证工艺参数对成形质量的影响。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the influence of laser power and scanning speed on the forming quality of high-layer-thickness Ti-6Al-4V parts fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: A systematic experimental approach was employed, varying laser power and scanning speed to assess their effects on density, defect formation, and mechanical properties.
summary_en.result: Optimal process parameter windows were identified, leading to improved forming quality of the SLM-produced Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary_en.validation: The findings were validated through experimental characterization of the fabricated specimens, including density and mechanical testing.
